- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- Overshoots after sharp upward spikes in the history (e.g., after 79.16 or 79.68), then corrects with a downward bias.
- Underestimates in the middle-to-late horizon (days 15–30) when true values show mean reversion toward lower levels.
- Forecasts tend to be too smooth; fails to capture volatility or sudden reversals in the last 5–7 days.
- Model exhibits lagged response: true values often exceed forecast by 1–3 days, suggesting a 1–2 day delay in adjusting to new data.
- When history includes a strong upward trend, model overreacts and forecasts higher than true outcome, especially if the trend is not sustained.
- Forecasts should be adjusted downward by 1–2% for the last 5–7 days if the history shows signs of mean reversion or downward pressure.
- Avoid overfitting to recent spikes; if last 3–5 days are high, reduce forecast by 2–5% to avoid overshoot.
- If true outcome shows a sharp drop after a spike, model should reduce forecast by 3–5% in the following 3–5 days to reflect mean reversion.
